by: product-os-keeper, for #1021 (reorganise the business intents): BI-9 (Orchestration) close
source: The product owner's approval of 2026-11-11, reply "approved", recorded in .garura/project/issues/1021/context/bi-9-close/approval.md, of the proposal in .garura/project/issues/1021/context/bi-9-close/proposal.md: one sentence added to the domain page's first paragraph, as the five capabilities of Orchestration stay in software delivery planning; and the domain sentence on those five capability pages, each with one Sources line quoting the domain page. BI-9's page is kept as it is.

changes.old: This domain turns a business intent into working code that a check from the outside can prove. It serves the product owner, who names the work, the technical lead, who designs it, and the developer, who builds it. It specifies the product, sets the project's design, and builds the work test first. It writes the eval that says if the work is met before the work is built, and it never gives a builder the eval or the tests: a check flags each build session that read them. It then tests the built work from outside the builder, by its evals and against the levels, surfaces, designs and standards set before the build. Once the product is in use, it takes in how the product is used, what people say about it and what its competitors do, works out what consumers want, and turns that into new features or changes to the model, as recommendations to the product owner or on their own where the product owner allows it. It also gets Garura itself into a project, sets the project up for it, keeps it current, and serves whichever coding tool the team works in. It also lands every change the same way, with an outside review and a person's yes, and gives people one tool to review what agents made. It does not release the work or run the product.
changes.new: This domain turns a business intent into working code that a check from the outside can prove. It serves the product owner, who names the work, the technical lead, who designs it, and the developer, who builds it. It specifies the product, sets the project's design, and builds the work test first. It writes the eval that says if the work is met before the work is built, and it never gives a builder the eval or the tests: a check flags each build session that read them. It then tests the built work from outside the builder, by its evals and against the levels, surfaces, designs and standards set before the build. Once the product is in use, it takes in how the product is used, what people say about it and what its competitors do, works out what consumers want, and turns that into new features or changes to the model, as recommendations to the product owner or on their own where the product owner allows it. It also gets Garura itself into a project, sets the project up for it, keeps it current, and serves whichever coding tool the team works in. It also lands every change the same way, with an outside review and a person's yes, and gives people one tool to review what agents made. It also orchestrates the work: it chooses and orders what runs next, runs plays as loops, tracks the work in the team's tracker, records each decision on how the project is built as an ADR, and gives every gate a way past. It does not release the work or run the product.

changes.old: It matters because a person can then always say what is happening and what comes next: in the intent's words, "A person always knows what's happening and what's next." It sits in software delivery planning for now. The domain's first paragraph does not yet say that the domain also runs the work; that is owed at the close of Orchestration.
